standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, the lemma that a dominant birational morphism to a normal scheme has structure sheaf pushforward the structure sheaf, and Cohomology of Schemes, the lemma that higher direct images vanish above the dimension of the fibres

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of higher cohomology of coherent sheaves on a modification

core_obligations: Compute the direct images (proof lines 1917-1938): since the source is normal and the morphism is dominant and birational, the pushforward of the structure sheaf is the structure sheaf; because the fibres have dimension at most one, the higher direct images above degree one vanish; the support of the first direct image is contained in the images of those components of the special fibre of the source which map to points of the special fibre of the base, a finite set of closed points because both special fibres are proper one dimensional schemes over the residue field; hence the first direct image is generated by global sections.

Deduce the sequence (proof lines 1938-1944): the vanishing of cohomology in degrees larger than one for coherent sheaves on the base scheme makes the Leray spectral sequence for the morphism and the structure sheaf degenerate to the stated short exact sequence, whose middle term is the first cohomology of the source.
proof_roadmap: Identify the zeroth and the higher direct images and locate the support of the first one.
Use global generation of the first direct image and cohomological vanishing on the base.
Read off the short exact sequence from the Leray spectral sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a modification between normal two dimensional schemes over a Noetherian normal local domain of dimension two, the first cohomology of the structure sheaf embeds into that of the modification with quotient the global sections of the first direct image, which is supported in finitely many closed points and generated by global sections (statement lines 1900-1915). The proof (proof lines 1917-1944) computes the relevant direct images, locates the support of the first one, and degenerates the Leray spectral sequence. H3: a spectral sequence argument with an analysis of the support, written out in full.
